newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa defends state oil company plans.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa defends state oil company plans.

text.p: South African Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna on Wednesday defended his plans to develop and strengthen a state oil company with black private sector and labour participation.

As he introduced his 1997/98 budget in parliament, Maduna dismissed recent criticism that his plans heralded a move towards nationalisation of the industry when government had committed itself to the privatisation of state assets.
"I find these negative reactions perplexing, as South Africa has had a state oil company for more than a quarter of a century, that is, the Central Energy Fund," he said.

He said CEF should be restructured to "create opportunities to bring into the liquid fuels industry, at critical levels, labour and those who in the pat...could not own equity in the entire industry."
He said what he planned was merely an extension of state-owned exploration company Soekor's joint venture with Energy Africa to develop the Oribi oil field.
Energy Africa owns 20 percent of the oilfield.
